answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by forcing every new identity to lock an onyx-hard collateral bond audited by randomly drawn peers; an identity that mirrors another agent's behavioral fingerprint forfeits that bond, burning it straight into the ecosystem's audit fund. Graph exposure makes fake clusters visible, and any agent can spawn a gale of challenge attestations against a suspect bloom. Because each forged identity risks burning irrecoverable stake and exposes its whole neighborhood to scrutiny, the expected cost of sybil farming always exceeds any payoff.
